data.title: Anthropic IPO Should Spark ‘Relief Rally’ In AI Stocks, Analyst Expects ‘Modest Hop’ On Day One
data.description:
Key points:
  • Meeks said Nvidia, Google and Broadcom should benefit because of their ties to Anthropic.
  • The analyst noted that Anthropic’s IPO is worth “participating in” even at $83, based on revenue growth.
  • Meeks added that the IPO may not change the bears’ focus on a collapse “multi years out.”

Paul Meeks, head of tech research at Freedom Capital Markets, said on Thursday that Anthropic’s (ANT) IPO could give AI stocks a lift after weeks of selling pressure, with companies tied to the AI infrastructure buildout among the potential beneficiaries.

“I would expect that you get some sort of relief rally in all these stocks based on this IPO, and I expect it to be up modestly,” Meeks said in an interview with CNBC. “I would expect a modest hop on the day.”

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the marketed range of $70 to $78. The company is expected to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The offering raised $81.3 billion.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ANT stock trended in ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past day, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ levels of chatter.

Anthropic IPO May Bring Relief To AI Stocks

Meeks stated that the stock may not see a dramatic first-day jump, partly because investors have had plenty of time to anticipate the offering. “Modest because you have a lot of excitement about this IPO, but it’s already been upsized, and it’s already been, you know, well discussed for a year or more,” he said.

He also does not expect Anthropic to reach a $2 trillion market capitalization by the end of its first trading session. “I don’t think that we will push by the end of trading day one a $2 trillion market cap,” he said. “But I think it’ll be welcome.”

Despite the higher-than-expected IPO price, Meeks said he believes the stock is worth participating in, pointing to the company’s revenue growth prospects.

“I think that the IPO will be very successful, and I think even where it was priced, you know, higher than the initial range from the investment bankers, I actually think it’s worth participating in, based on the revenue growth I see the next couple of years,” he said.

Meeks Sees Potential Lift For Nvidia, Google And Broadcom

Meeks expects the IPO to benefit companies with close ties to Anthropic, including Nvidia (NVDA), Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google and Broadcom (AVGO). “It should help Nvidia. It should help Google. It should help Broadcom because they have strong relationships with Anthropic,” he said.

He added that AI infrastructure stocks could be due for a rebound after a prolonged period of weakness. “I think overall, this should be a benefit, particularly since these AI infrastructure names, for the most part, have been deeply oversold in the last couple of weeks, last couple of months,” Meeks said.

NVDA stock rose 1.7% in pre-market trade, on track to break its five-day losing streak. GOOGL stock rose around 4%, and AVGO shares were up nearly 3%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Nvidia and Alphabet trended in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around Broadcom was in the ‘bullish’ zone.

According to Meeks, SpaceX (SPCX) is also among the companies that stand to benefit from Anthropic’s infrastructure spending because Anthropic has committed about $120 billion to SpaceX over the years, making the AI company’s ability to fund those obligations an important consideration for investors.

SPCX stock was up 2.3% in pre-market trade, with retail sentiment dipping to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day.

Wall Street Begins Anthropic Coverage With Bullish Ratings

Citizens, Melius Research and Wolfe Research initiated coverage of Anthropic with bullish ratings.

According to TheFly, Citizens and Wolfe both assigned Anthropic ‘Outperform’ ratings, with price targets of $125 and $135, respectively. Melius initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a $155 two-year price target, implying a potential upside of over 85% from the IPO price of $83.

Citizens cited Anthropic’s experienced management team and its ability to train and serve Claude across four major chip families. Melius sees a potential $40 trillion addressable market and expects the company’s projected 85% gross margins to support its substantial compute commitments.

Longer-Term AI Spending Concerns Remain

Meeks does not expect Anthropic’s public debut to put an end to the market’s broader concerns about the AI trade.

“I don’t know if that’s necessarily going to change the view of the doom and gloom cycle that we’ve been in at least the last couple of weeks, because none of the bears really are worried about anyone’s near-term fortunes,” he said. He added that they are concerned about “the collapse multi years out.”

Meeks also pointed to concerns about neocloud providers and companies that build or operate data-center capacity for AI customers. “I don’t think it's a legitimate threat,” he said, dismissing concerns around the AI colocation companies.

data.title: Kotak Life launches index-linked annuity plan targeting India’s growing retirement gap
data.description:
Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance Company on Wednesday launched the Kotak Variable Index Annuity Plan, a retirement product that links lifelong guaranteed income to the performance of the Nifty 50 Index. The plan is aimed at addressing longevity risk and inflation erosion, two concerns increasingly central to retirement planning in India.

The product offers guaranteed annuity rates fixed at inception, a return of premium on death, and higher annuity rates for longer deferment periods. Policyholders can benefit from index-linked growth tied to the Nifty 50, allowing income to potentially keep pace with rising living costs while retaining the security of a guaranteed payout for life.

Piyush Trivedi, Chief Distribution Officer at Kotak Life, cited demographic pressure as a key driver. India’s population aged 60 and above is projected to reach 347 million by 2050, he noted, making solutions that balance income certainty with inflation protection increasingly relevant.

The launch targets individuals in their 40s and 50s who understand their retirement corpus requirements but may not have saved enough to meet them. The company said demand is rising for hybrid products that offer both predictable income and purchasing power protection.

Kotak Life, a wholly owned subsidiary of Kotak Mahindra Bank, operates across 372 branches in 163 cities and has insured more than 50 million lives to date.

data.title: IndusInd Nippon Life Insurance posts 18% premium growth, eyes top-tier ranking in first year under new identity
data.description:
IndusInd Nippon Life Insurance Company Ltd. (INLIC) has reported 18 per cent new business premium growth and a net profit of ₹248 crore in FY2025-26, marking one year since its rebranding from Reliance Nippon Life Insurance under the ownership of IndusInd International Holdings Limited and Japan’s Nippon Life Insurance.

The Mumbai-headquartered insurer crossed ₹40,000 crore in Assets Under Management (AUM) in FY2025-26, maintained a claims settlement ratio of 98.94 per cent, and held a solvency ratio of 218 per cent, well above the regulatory minimum of 150 per cent.

Momentum carried into the first half of FY2026-27, with individual weighted regular premium growing 14 per cent, total premium reaching approximately ₹2,800 crore and AUM rising to ₹42,435 crore as of September 2026.

INLIC announced a bancassurance partnership with IndusInd Bank, which serves approximately 42 million customers across 3,137 branches. The company also launched an Integrated Channel distribution model, targeting presence in over 100 cities within two years, with a focus on Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. Additionally, its term insurance products are now available on PolicyBazaar’s platform.

The company serves over 10 million policyholders through 713 branches and 68,793 distributors. It declared a bonus of approximately ₹423 crore for participating policyholders in FY2025-26.

India’s life insurance penetration stands at around 3 per cent of GDP, below the global average, a gap INLIC is positioning itself to address through distribution expansion and digital investment.

data.description:
RNS Number : 9286D Trifast PLC 19 November 2026  

19 November 2026

TRIFAST PLC

(“Trifast” or the “Company”)

Capital Reduction Effective

Trifast plc (“Trifast” or the “Group”, LSE: TRI.L), the international specialist in the design, engineering, manufacture, and distribution of high-quality engineered fastenings, is pleased to announce that the capital reduction comprising the cancellation of the Capital Reduction Share and the cancellation of the amount standing to the credit of the Company’s share premium account (together, the “Capital Reduction”), approved by shareholders at the general meeting of the Company held on 14 October 2026 (the “General Meeting”), is now effective.

At the General Meeting, resolution 1 authorising the capitalisation of £16,329,085.00 of the Company’s merger relief reserve and the allotment and issue of the Capital Reduction Share, and resolution 2 approving the Capital Reduction, each as set out in the notice of the General Meeting dated 23 September 2026 (the “Notice”) (together, the “Capital Reduction Resolutions”), were duly passed by shareholders. Following the passing of the Capital Reduction Resolutions, the Company applied to the High Court for confirmation of the Capital Reduction. The High Court confirmed the Capital Reduction at a hearing held on 17 November 2026. The court order confirming the Capital Reduction and the statement of capital approved by the High Court have now been duly registered by Companies House.

Accordingly, the amount of £22,587,008.70 previously standing to the credit of the share premium account of the Company and the amount of £16,329,085.00, being the nominal value of the Capital Reduction Share, have been cancelled and have been credited to the retained earnings reserve of the Company, increasing the Company’s distributable reserves by £38,916,093.70 and providing flexibility for future dividends. The Capital Reduction has not resulted in any change to the nominal value or number of the Company’s ordinary shares in issue, has no impact on the Company’s cash position or net assets and has not involved any repayment or distribution of capital by the Company. The quantum and timing of any future returns of cash or capital will be at the discretion of the Board and will be dependent on the Company’s general working capital requirements and the amount and nature of its distributable reserves from time to time.

Capitalised terms used and not defined in this announcement have the meanings given to them in the Notice.

data.title: CoreWeave co-founder discloses bond purchase, says he will hold until maturity
data.description:
CoreWeave co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo disclosed late on Wednesday that he purchased some of the company's unsecured bonds and intends to hold them until maturity.

"Last week, I purchased $30 million in face value of CoreWeave’s unsecured bonds," Venturo wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "I intend to hold them to maturity on October 1, 2031. When we started CoreWeave, I couldn’t have imagined the scale of what our customers are building with us today. I believe in their work, and I’m proud of the team we’ve built to support it. I’ve never been more confident in CoreWeave."

Shares of the Livingston, N.J.-based company rose 5.8% in premarket trading on Thursday.

CoreWeave's debt has seen sharp drops in prices lately as investors become concerned about the neocloud industry's ability to survive if the artificial intelligence spending boom were to slow down.

Earlier this month, it was reported that CoreWeave was planning to raise at least $4B through an investment-grade loan, with Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group leading the potential financing. The proposed financing is expected to follow a structure backed by semiconductor chips and related customer contracts, allowing CoreWeave to borrow at a lower cost than through the high-yield debt market. The company has increasingly relied on asset-backed financing to fund its AI infrastructure expansion.

The move comes after CoreWeave raised its full-year revenue forecast, helping ease investor concerns about its debt-heavy business. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66B, up 168% year-over-year, and raised its 2026 revenue outlook to between $13B and $13.3B.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator also recently indicated that he has cancelled his 10b5-1 plan. A 10b5-1 is a pre-arranged stock trading plan that allows corporate insiders—such as CEOs and board members—to sell or buy company shares on a fixed schedule.

data.title: TSMC, Samsung Reportedly Suspend Some Chip Deliveries To Chinese Customers Amid New US Export Rules
data.description:
Key points:
  • Deliveries are paused while the chipmakers apply for licenses from the US Commerce Department, FT reported.
  • The new U.S. rules close a route that let Chinese chip designers obtain high-performance processors through independent packaging and testing firms.
  • Smartphone chip licenses would likely be approved, though the process could cause manufacturing delays, the report said.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) and Samsung Electronics have reportedly suspended shipments of certain semiconductors to Chinese customers following new U.S. export restrictions aimed at limiting Beijing’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips,

The chipmakers informed Chinese customers in recent days that deliveries would be paused while they apply for licenses from the US Commerce Department, the Financial Times reported Thursday, citing multiple people briefed on the matter.

​Stocktwits reached out to both Samsung and TSMC for comment but had not received a response from either company at the time of publication.

New Rules Close Chip Supply Route

The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) introduced new licensing requirements on Monday for certain advanced chips produced using American technology.

According to the publication, the changes close a pathway that allowed Chinese chip designers to obtain high-performance processors through independent packaging and testing companies.

​Previously, these companies could verify that chip designs fell outside US export restrictions, enabling shipments without direct government approval. The new requirements remove that route for affected Chinese customers, the report said.

​The restrictions add pressure to China’s technology sector, which is already facing rising memory chip prices and capacity constraints at domestic suppliers such as Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation.

Smartphone Chip Deliveries Also Affected

TSMC and Samsung have also notified consumer electronics customers of shipment suspensions, per the report. The new regulations eliminate exemptions previously used to establish that certain advanced chips were intended for non-AI applications, including smartphones.

Samsung’s Chinese customers include Baidu’s AI data-center chip unit Kunlun and TikTok parent ByteDance, both of which have sought alternative chip supplies amid shortages of Nvidia processors in China, the FT reported, but it did not establish that shipments to either company were specifically suspended.

Meanwhile, TSMC manufactures smartphone processors for Chinese companies including Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo.

An indutry insider told the FT that US authorities would likely approve licenses for consumer smartphone chips, but the licensing process could cause significant manufacturing delays. The timing of regulatory approvals remains uncertain, leaving manufacturers without clarity on when affected shipments can resume.

Retail Sentiment Around TSM Stock

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around TSM stock flipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ a day ago.

So far in 2026, TSM shares have gained more than 13%, while Samsung’s South Korea-listed shares have surged over 53%.

In comparison, the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL), which holds TSMC shares, and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), which holds Samsung shares, have risen more than 4% and 41% year-to-date, respectively.
